newsitem.title: INDIA: India's United Front willing to consider new chief.
newsitem.headline: India's United Front willing to consider new chief.

text.p: India's ousted United Front coalition said on Sunday it was willing to consider a demand by its rival Congress party to replace its leader, caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.

"I am not saying that a change in leadership is ruled out," a senior United Front official told reporters after a meeting of the coalition's decision-making Steering Committee. "Till yesterday, we were saying that a change in leadership is not negotiable."

Deve Gowda resigned on Friday after losing a vote of confidence in the lower house of parliament, and agreed to remain as caretaker Prime Minister. Until Sunday, the United Front had said there was no question of replacing Deve Gowda as coalition leader.
Congress, which precipitated Deve Gowda's fall by withdrawing its support, has said it would consider helping the United Front to form a new government provided the alliance dropped its leader.

Asked how the United Front and Congress could reach common ground to avert mid-term elections, the senior official said the decision-making Congress Working Committee (CWC), set to meet on Monday, would have to withdraw a written claim, given last month to President Shankar Dayal Sharma, to form a government.
"The CWC must make the formal offer. They must convey their latest decision to the president, which means a reversal of the earlier decision," the senior official said.
